text:
user_james: FYI customer on paid account hitting 400 when calling a tool via the API after pasting JSON from Windows cmd. They send: 'invalid JSON' from our gateway. Repro steps + raw payload below.

alice_support: can you paste the exact error and request id?

user_james: error 400 Bad Request - Invalid JSON at position 16. request_id=rid_0a1b2c3d4e

qa_marta: this screams Windows cmd expansion/escaping. if they use `echo {\"path\":\"%PATH%\"} > payload.json` cmd expands %PATH% and may insert unexpected chars. also cmd sometimes inserts CRLF (\r\n) and caret `^` escaping can get mixed in.

user_james: here's the payload they pasted (raw from customer):
```
{"filename":"user-data.json",\r\n
"args":"{\"path\":\"C:\\Program Files\\App%VERSION%\"}"
```
They said they created payload via `cmd` and then copy/pasted into the web UI.

dev_vijay: can you share the curl/request they sent to the API? need to see Content-Type and whether they used --data or --data-binary.

user_james: they used:
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data @payload.json https://api.redwood.example/v1/tools/run
```
When our gateway receives it the toolargs field contains literal CR (0x0D) and unescaped `%` sequences which our JSON parser treats as invalid in that context. Example parse error points at the percent sign inside a quoted string (we don't accept lone control bytes).

qa_marta: quick repro locally: create payload with CRLF via Notepad or cmd `echo ...... > file` then `curl --data @file`. Our parser error replicates. The underlying issue: Windows client produced a file encoded with CRLF and possibly a BOM or environment variable expansion inside the JSON string.

dev_vijay: mitigation suggestions to pass to customer: 1) Use PowerShell's `Set-Content -Path payload.json -Value (ConvertTo-Json $obj) -Encoding UTF8` or `curl --data-binary @payload.json` to avoid mangling; 2) ensure file saved as UTF-8 without BOM; 3) wrap tool args as base64 and decode server-side (temporary). I'll prepare a short snippet.

alice_support: please add the short snippet for customer (one-liner). Also create internal ticket.

dev_vijay: snippet for customer:
```
# PowerShell (no expansion, proper UTF-8)
$payload = @{ filename = 'user-data.json'; args = @{ path = 'C:\\Program Files\\App' } } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
Set-Content -Path payload.json -Value $payload -Encoding utf8
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @payload.json https://api.redwood.example/v1/tools/run
```
Or short temporary workaround: `jq -c . payload.json | base64 | xargs -I{} curl -H ... --data-binary "{}"` (server decode).

ops_bot: Incident created: INC-4578 - toolargs parser fails on Windows CRLF/%VAR% expansion in pasted JSON (priority: P3)

qa_marta: adding notes to INC-4578: reproduce steps, sample payloads, failing parser stack snippet, triage tags: parser, cli-client, windows, customer-impact.

dev_vijay: i'll add a small validation change to the parser to detect unescaped control chars (\r,\n) and unexpanded percent patterns inside quoted strings and return 422 with a helpful hint instead of generic 400. ETA: patch tomorrow EOD, will attach test vectors.

alice_support: thanks — i'll reply to the customer with the workaround and timeline. :thumbsup:

user_james: sending customer the PowerShell snippet now, will update once they confirm.

qa_marta: note for the eng team — also consider trimming trailing commas and smartly rejecting BOM. we saw a variant where Notepad saved with BOM and our parser choked.

dev_vijay: agreed. filing follow-up subtasks in INC-4578.

alice_support: closing loop here for now, moving to the ticket. :white_check_mark:
